title: Regional fallback negotiator & request slimming lanes
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: During cross-region failover and localized capacity pressure we need a more nuanced load-shedding mechanism that preserves high-value requests and reduces blast radius for tenant-facing SLOs. Current admission is coarse-grained token-bucket eviction and global circuit breakers; operators and product teams want predictable degradation modes that prefer regional affinity, honor tenant SLAs, and allow partial (trimmed) responses for lower-priority traffic.
summary: Implement a runtime component (the 'Fallback Negotiator') that mediates multi-region routing + admission decisions. It exposes per-tenant scoring and a set of 'concession lanes' — lightweight request slimming transforms (prefix trimming, role-based fidelity flags, model-variant downgrade) and priority queue admission (regional-affinity, SLA weight, realtime urgency). The negotiator runs before model selection and KV-cache lookup to maximize cost savings when shedding.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Negotiator component deployed to staging; can evaluate and return a per-request action (accept, delay, slim, fallback-to-variant, reject) within 2ms P50 in staging traffic
A2: Priority scoring uses tenant weight + request-level urgency + region affinity; documented config and defaults in the console
A3: Implement 3 concession lanes: response-trim, quantized-variant-fallback, and rate-window-deferral. Each lane must have a configurable budget and observable metrics
A4: During synthetic overload (60% above target QPS) system preserves 95% of P0 tenant tokens and sheds P3 traffic via slimming or variant fallback as configured
A5: End-to-end e2e test that simulates us-east failover to eu-west and shows negotiator prevents capacity thrash and maintains cross-region SLOs (latency and availability dashboards)
A6: Runbook updated with playbook for emergency overrides and rollback steps; stakeholders signed off (SRE, Product, Security)
tasks: Design: define scoring formula and default weights (SRE + Product workshop)
Prototype: implement negotiator service interface and lightweight policy DSL
Runtime: integrate negotiator with admission pipeline (pre-model selection hook)
Concession lanes: implement three slim transforms & model-variant routing
Observability: add metrics (negotiator decisions, per-lane budget consumption, latency), traces and Grafana dashboards
Testing: create chaos tests for multi-region failover and synthetic overload scenarios
Docs & Runbook: write console config UX spec, operator runbook, and security review notes
PRs: land prototype repo changes and runtime integration; coordinate canary in staging
decisions: D1: Negotiator will be deployed as a sidecar-capable service in the serving runtime host, not a central control plane service, to avoid single-point-of-failure and reduce RTT cost
D2: Scoring formula will be additive: tenant_weight (0-100) + urgency_bonus (0-50) + region_affinity_bonus (0-30) - current_node_pressure_penalty (0-100). Values are tunable via console
D3: Concession lanes are applied in order of cost-benefit: (1) response-trim, (2) quantized-variant-fallback, (3) rate-window-deferral; each lane must be reversible or retriable
D4: We will expose a tenant-facing SLA weight that customers can opt into via Console; default is 50 for free tier, 80 for paid tier
D5: Circuit breaker interaction: negotiator can route to a lower-cost region/model if local circuit breaker is tripped, but will not route cross-region if data-locality flag is set for the tenant
tradeoffs: T1: Sidecar deployment increases per-host resource usage and operational complexity vs. central service simplicity; we chose availability and latency over operational uniformity
T2: Slimming transforms risk output quality degradation; to minimize customer impact we only apply them to P2/P3 requests and provide evaluation hooks in onboarding
T3: More aggressive shedding improves latency for high-value tenants but increases errors for lower tiers — we add observability and an SLA-weight opt-out to balance expectations
T4: Keeping the negotiator decision fast constrains how complex scoring can be; we favor small, tunable arithmetic over ML models for initial rollout
notes: Meeting 2026-02-12: SRE + Product prioritized this as top reliability initiative for multi-region churn scenarios
Prototype doc: see design sketch in Confluence and image of decision flow
Security: list of allowed transformations vetted by Security (no PII stripping; only length/variant adjustments)
Data residency: tenants can set data_locality=true to prevent cross-region fallback
